name: AgentForge: GenAI Studio
tag: Build multi-agent workflows with retrieval, tools and monitoring, then ship them with a ready deployment plan.

scenarios.title: HR policy answer agent
scenarios.ask: Build an agent that answers HR policy questions from our {pages}-page handbook for {staff} employees.
steps: Ingest
Indexed the {pages}-page handbook into {=round(pages * 4.9)} searchable passages.
Builder
Created an answer agent and a checker agent that verifies every citation.
Test
Ran {tests} sample questions. {=tests - ceil(tests * 0.04)} correct with page citations, {=ceil(tests * 0.04)} sent to HR.
Deploy
Generated a deployment blueprint with logging and a monthly accuracy report.
followups: What happens when the handbook changes?
Upload the new version and the Ingest step re-indexes only the changed pages. The test set re-runs automatically before the update goes live.
Can it see salary or personal records?
No. It only reads the documents you give it. Personal questions are routed to HR by the checker agent.
How much HR time could it save?
If each question takes HR about 6 minutes, {=round(staff * 0.3)} questions a month is roughly {=round(staff * 0.3 * 6 / 60)} hours. Treat that as an estimate until you have a month of logs.

scenarios.title: Sales research assistant
scenarios.ask: Build a workflow that researches {accounts} target accounts a week and drafts a brief for each rep.

inputs.label: Tools to call (CRM, web search, news...)

steps: Builder
Set up a Researcher agent with {tools} tools and a Writer agent that turns notes into a one-page brief.
Retrieval
Connected past call notes so briefs mention earlier conversations.
Monitor
Added tracing for every tool call and a cost cap per brief.
Test
Ran 10 sample accounts. Reps rated 8 briefs ready to use, 2 needed edits.
Deploy
Scheduled the workflow for Monday mornings.
followups: Where does the 20 minutes per account come from?
It is a typical time for a rep to research an account by hand. Replace it with your team's number for a better estimate.
Yes. A thumbs up or down on each brief is logged, and the monthly report shows which sections get edited most.

scenarios.title: Move a prototype to production
scenarios.ask: We have a notebook prototype. Get it ready for {users} users with a {sla} response target.
steps: Importer
Turned the notebook into a workflow with 4 named steps.
Load test
Simulated {users} users. Peak of about {=ceil(users * 0.02)} requests a minute.
Optimizer
Added caching for repeat questions and a smaller model for routing to hit {sla}.
Blueprint
Wrote the deployment plan: {=max(2, ceil(users / 4000 * 10 / sla))} replicas, alerts and a rollback step.
followups: Which cloud does the blueprint target?
It can target AWS, Azure or Google Cloud. The workflow itself stays the same, only the deployment files change.
Error rate or latency above your limit for 5 minutes, or a drop in the quality score on the live test set.
